reviews.author: ohyes ohyes
reviews.text:
Visited 3 times in March 2024.
There is no separate parking lot and it seems difficult to find paid parking.

I visited on three consecutive weekday evenings. In the early evening hours, you had to wait in line for about an hour, but if you went after 8 p.m., you could enter almost immediately without waiting in line.
I thought it was a kalguksu restaurant because hand kalguksu came first in the name of the restaurant, but the bossam was the main dish and the kalguksu felt like dessert. On the first day, two adult men visited and ordered a set meal for two and potato pancakes.
Side dishes included cabbage, radish kimchi for bossam, and cabbage kimchi. It seemed like cabbage could be refilled if it ran out. I'm not sure if it's possible, but since I ate all the cabbage, I didn't ask for it separately, but they brought me another plate. Bossam came out first and kimchi was served on the same plate as bossam. In other words, a total of 3 plates of kimchi were served, including radish kimchi and 2 plates of cabbage kimchi. The bossam was served with just the right amount of meat and fat, and it was quite soft and well-cooked without any unpleasant smell. The kimchi was spicy and sweet just right for bossam, so when I wrapped the kimchi in bossam, the seasoning went really well and it was delicious. As of March 24, one set meal costs 15,000 won, and the taste is good and the quantity is large, so it can be said to be really good value for money. There was enough food for two adult men to be full. One bowl of rice is provided per person, but only about half of the rice is served. It seemed like only half of the kalguksu noodles were served, but I ate all of the kalguksu noodles and mixed the rice with the soup and it was delicious. The kalguksu is meat kalguksu, but perhaps because of the pepper, it was not greasy, but rather had a refreshing feeling, as if you were refreshing your mouth after eating bossam. That said, it doesn't taste as refreshing as seafood kalguksu, but it was refreshing, perhaps because it was after eating bossam. Potato pancakes have a savory and oily taste, so I think they would be really delicious to eat while having a drink. If you look around, there are a lot of people drinking alcohol.

This is a place I want to visit often. If you are not a big eater, you can add potato pancakes or seafood and green onion pancakes to the set meal for two people, or for three to four people or more. It's a bit much to add for 2 people.

reviews.author: Sung Kettler
reviews.text: The most delicious restaurant during my two-week visit to my hometown. The unobtrusive signboard and interior reminiscent of the 80s and 90s gave me a very nostalgic feeling as I spent my childhood around that time. I visited after reading a blog post recommending a delicious restaurant by an office worker near Seongsu.  It was an odd time at 2pm, so there was no waiting. The table setting is simple (boiled pork, cabbage, dried radish, 2 types of kimchi, garlic, soybean paste, salted shrimp), but when I put the boiled pork, dried radish, kimchi, garlic salted shrimp on top of the cabbage and put it in my mouth, an unexpected feast of flavors suddenly unfolded. I don't like food that is overly sweet or seasoned(?), but it doesn't taste like the seasoning, and the ingredients come together and are crunchy and vibrant. It tasted sweet, but it wasn't artificial, just a pleasant level of sweetness. As we ate, they also gave us a bowl of kalguksu, but since I ate only a small portion, I almost left some of the kalguksu. Wouldn't it be better to give only half of the kalguksu and only give more if requested? Is it worth 15,000 won after eating this delicious food!? I was so grateful... I was so touched that my mouth got red all over my mouth while I was eating so hard that the owner's son ran out to me without saying a word and even gave me a tissue to wipe my mouth. To sum it up in a word, [I ate with tears in my mouth] On this day, I felt guilty about leaving the delicious food, so I ate too much, then canceled all of my afternoon plans and just slept in the hotel due to hunger, but I thought it was a worthless afternoon. The owner and his son were very kind and humble people, so it was a special experience that conveyed the emotion I felt from my mouth to my heart. I only deducted one star from Atmosphere because the atmosphere was too familiar to go on a date with a nice guy or girl.

reviews.author: Gu Kim
reviews.text:
5 minutes walk from Ttukseom Station
I visited with interest after seeing a review of Bibim Jjamppong on YouTube, but perhaps because it was lunch time, the tables were full even though I arrived around 11:50.
You can order menus using the tablet at your seat, pickled radish and onion cubes can be eaten in small portions from the side dish container on each table, and bring your own water! Haha
There were 3 employees in the kitchen and 1 in the hall, but since the order was placed on a tablet, the wait wasn't that long and there was no inconvenience.
Maybe it was because I had high expectations for Bibim Jjamppong, but when I ate it, it wasn't as delicious as wow.
The bibim jjamppong was not spicy or spicy and felt a bit bland, which was surprising, but it still tasted above average. The sauce has the loose texture of Manghyang bibim noodles rather than the consistency of stir-fried jjamppong. It is mixed from the time it is served, so there is no need to mix it separately.
Goppae is not on the separate menu, but you can order it without additional charge if you tell the hall employee after ordering at the kiosk.
The overall price goes up by 1,000 won, so it's not cheap for a Chinese restaurant. Considering the cost-effectiveness and taste, I would visit again.

reviews.author: Roberto Jeong-heum Yeon
reviews.text:
The crab, squid, and wood ear mushrooms in Jjamppong are excellent.

Jjamppong soup has a spicy aftertaste, so it seems they use a lot of finely ground red pepper powder.

I think the green noodles are chlorella noodles.

However, I don't know if I am confident enough in the taste of Jjamppong to call it "Bong "Jjamppong".

So, does it have excellent volume? That's not it either.

It's just a pity that the owner spent all his raw material costs on three things: blue crab, wood ear mushroom, and squid.

If the taste is not so differentiated that it overwhelms everything else, shouldn't it at least have the volume to fill the stomachs of common people?

Mussels, cabbage, and onions piled high without any seasoning. The volume, which seems abundant for the price, is an indispensable attraction when it comes to food. This means that it is a problem that cannot be solved with just a few sides.

That's why the jjamppong at my local Chinese restaurant adds at least the cheap, thick pine cone cut of Chilean squid.

Hotel Jjamppong and Chinese Cuisine, which are at the worst with trashy cost-effectiveness, are trying so hard not to lose volume through ingredients other than cotton in their Jjamppong.

But this volume at this price? It looks like you spent all your money on fresh crab.

Stir-frying it on the spot does not make it delicious and high-quality jjamppong. There are many restaurants where the Jjamppong broth is sufficiently delicious even if it is pre-boiled.

Especially if it is a problem that directly affects turnover or cost-effectiveness by increasing the cooking process or affecting material costs, why not give up your stubborn craftsmanship? Or how about comparing it with a two-track strategy?

If you see most of the customers eating Jjajang at a restaurant that serves Jjamppong... wouldn't it be right for the owner to think about it at least once?

I would rather ask what Bongjjajang is like.

I wonder if this place would be so crowded if there was only one reasonably priced Chinese restaurant around here.

Ah, but the fried dumplings were pretty tasty.

My wife and I decided to go to a well-rated Vietnamese restaurant and were excited. When we arrived, no one was there to greet us, so we tried to find a seat ourselves. All the tables we approached were dirty. As I was looking around for a while, an employee came out from behind the kitchen counter and showed me to my seat. The staff was very cold and seemed like they wanted to be somewhere else. Her attitude was so unfriendly that my wife didn't even notice her and continued looking for a clean table. Then the employee screamed at his wife. But the table was still dirty. We ended up wiping the table ourselves.

Ordering and paying for food was done using a tablet placed on the table. We tried to place an order, but the "Place Order" button was disabled. I was reluctant to call the staff. I suggested we just leave, but eventually decided to call him. The staff member reluctantly came to our table and tried to solve the problem. I unplugged the tablet and plugged it back in, and the order button started working. She trudged back to the miserable noodle shop and we tried to pay by card. But it didn't work again. I was afraid to call her out, but I had already gone too far. She came to us and tried again the same way we had already done. I asked if I could pay in cash (like the old days). She said no. She tried the card near the register and then came back to us and said there was a problem with the card. This was the first time I had an argument over credit card issues while traveling in Korea. Then I asked if I could pay in cash. I said it was okay. The food came out and it tasted pretty good. But I felt her hostility stronger than the taste of the food. It was truly the worst service experience in a long time. I would definitely not recommend this restaurant unless you are someone who enjoys mediocrity and pain.

reviews.text:
Flavor Town.

Ordered Matdongsan’s signature 3-person set.
The silken tofu salad seems to contain perilla leaves and chamnamul (?) as seasonal vegetables. Chili oil is added to the soft and mild-tasting silken tofu, giving it a flavor highlight.
Matdongsan fried dumplings are not particularly delicious as fried dumplings, but are delicious when eaten with sauce.
The fried pig's feet show an effort to reinterpret pig's feet in a new way. I think the pig's feet were disassembled like a fold fork, then placed in a mold and fried. It has an intuitive sweet and salty taste. It looks similar to head meat, but because it is fried, only the outside is slightly crispy and the skin and meat of the pig's trotters are soft. And the scent of cilantro in the strong sauce refreshes your mouth.
The Typhoon Shelter shrimp were crunchy due to the soybean cereal, but the shrimp shell itself was a bit tough. And it felt like there was a lot of cereal.
Emperor curry contains lobster and clams. The sauce is not just curry, but various spices are added, so it tastes reminiscent of Hong Kong or Southeast Asia.
One of the two desserts from Matdongsan is yuzu basil sorbet, and the other is mango, which is a cake-like dessert made with cold sheets.
The yuzu basil sorbet had a strong acidity, and the other dessert was like an ice cream sandwich, but it was hard and difficult to cut, and the taste itself was just so-so.
The taste itself isn't that bad, but the overall quantity is small.

The restaurant appears to have a second and third floor.
There doesn't seem to be a separate elevator.
The neon sign-like lights of the electronic display board inform the restaurant's identity and at the same time create a contemporary atmosphere.
It seems they mainly come for dates or gatherings.
It also looks good with accompaniment.
The clerk explains the menu in detail.

Intention to revisit) Average.

reviews.text:
I visited after making a reservation for Catch Table, but I don't think I'll be coming again.
The warm aperitif bread is really delicious, but unfortunately that's all.
In order of photo, they are Bolpo, Anello, and Paccheri Vongole.

I was very disappointed with the Bbpo. To put it bluntly, it had no octopus texture and had a strong smell. Is the Buppo I used to eat here much different from the Buppo here? As soon as I took a bite, I was a bit shocked.
Lamb ribs (Anello) are all cooked differently, some are too salty, and some are overcooked and tough. When I was eating the last piece, I could even smell the lamb.
Vongole is salty. Very salty.
There was a scoop of tiramisu for a review event, so I applied for it, but when I saw the food, I didn't want to eat it at all, so I didn't get it and just left.

The person in my group also criticized the overall food as being too salty and especially the boppo.
I think this is the first time I remember wasting money while eating Italian.
High prices without even following the basics... It's not easy.

I want to go next time I get the chance

reviews.author: HS

2020/10/10

It is said to be a hot store that opened a month ago!
With Jeju Island as a motif, the menu features Jeju Island food and the interior is decorated with a Jeju Island feel haha.
It's difficult to get into the Seoul Forest For Hue building, but it's not easy to find room 108, so I'm going to go to a private house. If you go through what looks like a staff-only door, there's a store...!

- The store has 6 comfortable table seats and 6 narrow counter seats, so I recommend making a reservation.
- The kitchen is completely open, so you can see everything being cooked right in front of you.
- Even though it hasn't been long since opening, there are a lot of customers and it's hot!
Is it because a pretty good Western restaurant has opened up around here?

💜
I ate gnocchi and Jeju marinated salt pasta!🍝🍽🥂
Both were delicious, and gnocchi suited my style better^0^
Wow, but I think the portion is a bit small. I ate it really quickly,,, I think I can eat it all if I wrap the spicy pasta around my fork 3-4 times to exaggerate.....
The gnocchi is also a bit small in quantity.
Anyway, the food was delicious, and perhaps because it was early in the opening period, they even gave us a white wine glass and they were friendly and nice!!

I plan to visit again~ I plan to try the black pork dish and rose pasta!

reviews.author: Isomsom
reviews.text:
I had a disappointing experience at this restaurant. I had originally made a reservation for two people, but due to a change in plans, I tried to call the restaurant the day before (over five times) to update the reservation to one person. No one picked up.

When I arrived alone, I was informed that the deposit for the second guest was non-refundable and takeaway was not allowed. While I could accept the policy, the staff’s attitude was the bigger issue. Phrases like “You should’ve called us yesterday,” “We were open, you didn’t call,” and “Even if you called, it was too late” were said in a dismissive and accusatory tone.

I explained I had indeed tried calling several times, but was essentially told that it didn’t matter. There was no real apology—just a repeated insistence that “There was nothing we could do.”

Service throughout the meal was also lacking. I ordered two pastas, one dessert, and a soda, but was only given one ice cup. When I asked for another, I was told they only provide one per drink.

The food was fine, but the overall customer service and rigid attitude made it an unpleasant experience. For a restaurant that requires deposits and operates on a reservation basis, I expected a much more thoughtful and professional approach.

I made a reservation for two people through the reservation system, but due to my group's schedule the day before, I had to visit alone, so I called the reservation number several times (more than five times in total), but I was never able to get through. I had no choice but to visit alone, and after arriving, I explained the situation, but was informed that “the reservation fee for one person is not refundable” and “take-out is not possible.”
I could understand up to this point, but after that, I was very disappointed in the attitude of the staff (chef and staff).

“I will do that for you,” “You should have called me in advance yesterday,” “You called yesterday? We were open for business as usual?”, “Anyway, even if you called yesterday, you were late,” etc. I was very offended by the high-handed tone and response that avoided responsibility throughout the conversation.
Despite telling them that they had called, the attitude of repeatedly assuming that they did not do it felt like they were distrusting the customer, and even after explaining the situation, the response was not flexible at all, ending with a firm tone such as "I'm just telling you that we couldn't help it," rather than a sincere apology.

The food was okay, but the overall service mindset and attitude was at a level that made customers not want to come back.
Also, even though I ordered two pasta dishes, a dessert, and a drink, there was a lack of consideration in even the smallest details, such as receiving only one ice cup and receiving a regular cup, saying that they could only provide as many ice cups as the number of drinks.

In the end, I changed my plan to eat alone and quickly called a friend to eat with me, but overall it was a very unpleasant experience and I didn't feel any consideration. If you're a restaurant that takes reservations, shouldn't you have a minimum level of responsiveness and flexibility?

reviews.author: Emily Beres
reviews.text:
If you are a vegetarian, this is a great place for a salad lunch. Just order your menu at the kiosk and fill it with toppings at the self-service bar. There are so many delicious menus.
Delicious and fresh!

Using the kiosk on the left, you can order with three options: just rice and salad, or just salad. Proteins such as meat or avocado can be added as an option. Please tell us whether you would like to eat in or take out. You must call 010 when ordering, and they say you will receive a text message when your order is ready. When your order number is called, go to the salad bar. It's completely self-service, so you can take as much as you want (but only one serving at a time). Alternatively, you can take only as much as you can fit in your bowl. All menu items here are vegan. There are other sauces like cucumber, chickpea, hummus, red cabbage, carrot (spicy) and basil, as well as falafel, roasted cauliflower and vegan fried nuggets.

All vegetables on the menu come with pepper dressing (vegan) as standard, so if you don't want it, please let the staff know in advance.

Overall, I think it's a good place. It's probably better suited for lunch, but it's a good choice if you want a healthy salad bowl type of diner and a 'build your own' option. There is plenty of seating in a bright and airy space. The most basic menu costs 12,000 won, and although the food isn't super delicious, it's worth it! The process of getting food can be a bit complicated for first-time visitors, but the staff are happy to help.

Refer to previous reviews - there is no additional charge for vegan food, and there seems to be no shakshuka at all.

reviews.author: A house that only tastes good
reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in hamburgers
Located a 4-minute walk from Exit 7 of Ttukseom Station.
The hangover burger set costs 11,800 won.

Grill burger?
Looking at the picture, it looks like the patties are grilled rather than pressed.
The patty was relatively thick, but there was no taste of grill fire.
Burger: bun, patty, cheese, onion, and hui-pung sauce
It tastes slightly spicy. Ramen soup? It feels the same.
It takes away the greasiness of the burger slightly.
Of course, the taste of the sauce is strong, so the original taste of the burger is slightly reduced.
Depending on the sauce, each person seems to have their own likes and dislikes.
The fries are a bit thick like Burger King.
It has a slightly sour taste, but I personally like it!
It's okay to eat it on its own or with ketchup.
The drinks come in cans so you can enjoy the original taste.

Store & Tips & Burgers
The store is not small and there are quite a few tables.
It is okay to eat alone and you can also enter with your dog.
Be careful if you have a dog allergy!
Order and pay at the kiosk at the entrance.
The interior of the store is clean and good for dining.
You can also bring pickles, etc. from the self-service bar.
There are a variety of burgers to choose from, so it's fun to eat them.
I visited at 2pm the day before Lunar New Year and the store was spacious~

reviews.author: JOOWON PARK
reviews.text: Well, I only ate the Gordon Ramsay burger 3 times, but the burger here was so delicious that I was blown away. Don't go overboard with the new menu. The cheeseburger is amazing. It's not greasy (perhaps because of the pepper flakes?), the patty is thick and juicy, and the burger bun itself is delicious. If you scrape off the onion glaze underneath, it tastes delicious, and the Seoul Forest Burger is also really good!! There's just the right amount of truffle-infused cream, and it's the size of a slice burger, so you can eat it cleanly, but the arugula is also generous and has a nice scent. I think I'll eat the same combination again next time I visit... The fries are high-quality with a lot of potato flavor, and the self-bar pickles are also delicious. Maybe it was because it was snowing that day, but the deliveries came like a joke, right? I'm going to find a good restaurant!!

reviews.author: Jo Min-jeong
reviews.text:
I like homemade burgers, so I went to all the burger restaurants in Seongsu, which has a lot of restaurants, and they were delicious when steamed! It's located a bit inside an alley, so it feels like a secret restaurant that only people in the know can visit 👀

The store is large, so group visits are possible, and the camping-style interior is clean and allows for fire pits in the evening (!).
​
The overall white tone makes it look spacious and cool, but the black, red, and steel accents make it look modern 🤔 It also had a Gordon Ramsey burger interior feel.

I ordered the Seoul Forest Burger Set with the Overflow Burger alone, upgraded the drink to lemonade, and the French fries with beef chili sauce.

Cheese poured right in front of you and cheese powder sprinkled on top! This is not tasty! The homemade burger was so thick that it was difficult to bite into it, but it was easier to eat because it was sliced.
​
If you like cheese, be sure to try it!
Is this the taste of mainland America? 🫢 (I’m not going to the US)

Seoul Forest Burger was the most basic burger, but the buns were delicious and the vegetables were fresh, so it was much more delicious than any American handmade burger brand I've tried, regardless of cost-effectiveness 👍

The fries are thick and really delicious! The chili sauce made with ground beef is recommended as it is deliciously spicy even for spicy eaters.

I ordered the Signature Burger, Big Ban Burger, Eggplant, Fried Chicken Feet, Melon Tart, S'mores Cookie, Schisandra Highball, and Zero Cola.
It's the most delicious hamburger I've ever had. It takes quite a long time for the food to come out.
The roe potatoes were mashed roe potatoes, full of truffle flavor and seasoned with sauce. It was a healthy snack, but it was very delicious. Even my younger brother, an elementary school student who doesn't eat vegetables or vegetables well, enjoyed it.
The signature burger's sauce was delicious, the patty was delicious, and the crunchy pickles were unusual, but they went well together and were delicious. After tasting it, I understood why it was famous for its burgers.
The Big Van Burger was not good. It had sedum and white bread and had an unusual appearance, but the taste was so difficult to understand that it had no impact, so I left it.
The fried chicken feet were eye-poppingly delicious. Spicy fried chicken feet that were crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside with a generous amount of cilantro. The refreshing grapefruit cut out the greasiness and went well with the cilantro. It was a great dish. I was very satisfied.
I ordered a melon tart for dessert. The melon was sweet, but it didn't go well with the tart, and it tasted different from the cream, so I didn't want to eat it again.
The s'mores cookies were hard, crumbly and tasteless compared to how they looked. The desserts were all bad.
I drank 3 cans of Zero Coke. It was so carbonated, and the Schisandra chinensis highball was made sweet, so I enjoyed it.
I plan to visit again, and I still want to eat there again. I was well and was full.
